by
  -- Use the tendsto_harmonic_sub_log lemma to show that harmonic n - log n approaches Euler-Mascheroni constant
  -- For sufficiently large n, harmonic n ≥ log n - γ, and since log(n+1) ≤ log n + 1/n, we can bound the difference
  -- We use the fact that Euler-Mascheroni constant is approximately 0.5772, so for n ≥ 1, 1/n + γ < 1
  -- Thus, harmonic n ≥ log n - γ ≥ log(n+1) - (1/n + γ)
  -- Therefore, harmonic n ≥ log(n+1)
  -- For small n, we can verify directly
  intro n,
  have h : Real.eulerMascheroniConstant ≈ 0.5772 := by decide_numeral,
  have h1 : 1 / n + Real.eulerMascheroniConstant < 1 := by linarith,
  have h2 : Real.log ↑(n + 1) ≤ ↑(harmonic n) :=
    by {
      cases n,
      case zero { simp },
      case succ n' { 
        -- Use the tendsto_harmonic_sub_log lemma
        -- The limit of harmonic n - log n is Real.eulerMascheroniConstant
        -- So for sufficiently large n, harmonic n ≥ log n - γ
        -- And since log(n+1) = log n + log(1 + 1/n) ≤ log n + 1/n
        -- Then harmonic n ≥ log n - γ ≥ log(n+1) - (1/n + γ)
        -- Hence harmonic n ≥ log(n+1)
        exact Real.tendsto_harmonic_sub_log.mp (Filter.atTop) (nhds Real.eulerMascheroniConstant) n
          (by simpa [Real.log_add] using Real.log_div_le_sum_range_add 0 1 n)
      }
    },
  exact h2
